name: Madhur Sree Madanantheshwara–Siddhivinayaka Temple
tagline: Riverside Madhur shrine — Madanantheshwara and Siddhivinayaka, famed for appa prasadam and living ritual-astrology practice
summary: Riverside Shiva–Ganesha shrine at Madhur near Kasaragod, known for its gajaprishta sanctum, daily appa prasadam and rare Moodappa Seva; a living centre for festival ritual and traditional prasna…
description: Madhur Sree Madanantheshwara–Siddhivinayaka Temple sits on the banks of the Madhuvahini (Mogral) river about 7–8 km from Kasaragod town. Formally a Shiva temple (Madanantheshwara), the south-facing swayambhu Ganapathi (Siddhivinayaka) in the main sanctum draws large crowds and gives the complex its popular name.

The temple architecture features a three-tiered gajaprishta (elephant-back) sreekovil, carved woodwork and a traditional chuttambalam; the riverside setting and ritual layout make it a notable heritage site in northern Kerala.

Madhur remains a living ritual centre: daily Udayasthamana offerings, the temple's signature appa (unniyappam) prasadam and large sevas such as Sahasrappa and the rare Moodappa Seva shape devotional life. Local tradition and temple practice also link the shrine to classical temple astrology — Deva‑Prashna and Ashta‑Mangalya enquiries are part of the region’s ritual repertoire.

Visitors get darshan, free appa prasadam queues, seasonal festivals (Madhur Bedi in Meenam, Vinayaka Chaturthi, Vishu and Maha Shivaratri) and the chance to see living ritual forms tied to folk memory and astrological decision‑making; confirm special sevas and timings with temple authorities before you travel.
highlights: Riverside setting on the Madhuvahini (Mogral) river
Three-tiered gajaprishta (elephant‑back) sreekovil and carved Namaskara Mandapam
Famous daily appa (unniyappam) prasadam and Sahasrappa (1,001 appa) offering
Moodappa (Moodappam) Seva — rare ceremony of coating the Ganapathi with appam
Living festival cycle (Madhur Bedi, Vinayaka Chaturthi) and daily Udayasthamana rites
Traditional links to Deva‑Prashna / Ashta‑Mangalya astrological enquiries

sections.heading: Background
body: Madhur is an ancient temple town in the Mayipadi (Kumbla) area; local tradition records a swayambhu Shiva linga found by a villager and the later emergence of the Ganapathi image from a child’s drawing. The present complex blends Kerala temple form with Tulu‑Nadu influences and is one of the principal pilgrimage shrines of northern Kerala.

Stories such as the Tipu Sultan sword‑mark on the temple well and the growing Ganapathi figure belong to local tradition and explain ritual practices like Moodappa Seva and the centrality of appa prasadam.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Darshan the Madanantheshwara linga and the south‑facing Siddhivinayaka; view the carved wooden ceilings and stucco work in the namaskara mandapam and walk the pradakshina path to see subsidiary shrines (Kashi Vishwanatha, Ayyappa, Durga, Subrahmanya).

Try the temple appa prasadam (unniyappam) at the prasadam counters; if a special seva (Sahasrappa, Udayasthamana or Moodappa) is scheduled, expect large crowds and advance booking/confirmation from the temple office.

Observe living ritual practices: monthly Sankashti, Vinayaka Chaturthi observances and annual Madhur Bedi festival (Meenam/Mar–Apr). Ask locally about any ongoing Deva‑Prashna or astrological consultations — these are a traditional way devotees and management seek ritual guidance.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Temple access: the site is roughly 7–8 km from Kasaragod town. Nearest major railhead is Kasaragod station; airports are Mangaluru (north, ~50 km) and Kannur (south). Local buses, taxis and autos connect Kasaragod and Madhur.

Practicalities: the temple usually opens early morning and closes in the evening with a midday break — timings vary on festival days, so confirm in advance. Photography is often restricted near the sanctum; follow dress code and temple staff instructions. If you travel for a special seva (e.g., Sahasrappa, Moodappa), confirm dates and booking with the temple office before you go.

latest.text: After a gap of 33 years the rare Moodappa (Moodappam) Seva was staged at Madhur in April 2025, reviving the temple’s signature large‑scale offering tradition.

visitorInfo.bestTime: October–February for pleasant weather; visit Meenam (March–April) for the temple’s annual Madhur Bedi festival; avoid heavy monsoon (June–September).
visitorInfo.howToReach: From Kasaragod town (7–8 km) by local bus, taxi or auto; nearest rail Kasaragod station; nearest airports Mangaluru International (~50 km north) and Kannur International (~100+ km south); allow time for return transport on festival days.
etiquette: Confirm special sevas, festival dates and darshan timings with the temple office before travelling.
Dress modestly in Kerala temple style (mundu/saree or conservative clothes); follow any dress rules posted at the temple.
Photography is often restricted inside the sanctum; ask permission and expect queues on Vinayaka Chaturthi and Madhur Bedi.
Bring small change for offerings and prasadam counters; arrive early for Udayasthamana or noon maha pooja to avoid long waits.
